### Morningstar Research Projects Universal Automated Savings Policies Could Improve Retirement-Income Adequacy


November 12, 2026


*Share of Gen Z, millennial, and Gen X households projected to cover expenses in retirement could rise 8 percentage points, from 59% to 67%*


CHICAGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[Morningstar,](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.morningstar.com%2F&esheet=54640339&newsitemid=20261112237920&lan=en-US&anchor=Morningstar%2C&index=1&md5=32bcab5a0360382cc1e551c9da8f3cea) Inc. (Nasdaq: MORN), a leading provider of independent investment insights, today released “[From Access to Adequacy: Modeling Universal Automated Savings](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.morningstar.com%2Fbusiness%2Finsights%2Fresearch%2Ffrom-access-to-adequacy-modeling-universal-automated-savings&esheet=54640339&newsitemid=20261112237920&lan=en-US&anchor=From+Access+to+Adequacy%3A+Modeling+Universal+Automated+Savings&index=2&md5=2db2f2ab25c1130139e63c5d66005621) ,” a new analysis from[Morningstar’s Center for Retirement & Policy Studies](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.morningstar.com%2Fbusiness%2Finsights%2Fretirement%2Fcenter-for-retirement-and-policy-studies&esheet=54640339&newsitemid=20261112237920&lan=en-US&anchor=Morningstar%26%238217%3Bs+Center+for+Retirement+%26amp%3B+Policy+Studies&index=3&md5=0a2379024fe0dd85afa9865e89e8be60) examining how federal savings policies could help more Americans prepare financially for retirement.


Researchers used[Morningstar’s Model of U.S. Retirement Outcomes](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.morningstar.com%2Fbusiness%2Flp%2Fmodel-of-us-retirement-outcomes&esheet=54640339&newsitemid=20261112237920&lan=en-US&anchor=Morningstar%26%238217%3Bs+Model+of+U.S.+Retirement+Outcomes&index=4&md5=b84d1661bc3eb5beae63713436d28b1f) to evaluate a combined policy scenario reflecting ideas under discussion among policymakers and policy experts, rather than a specific legislative proposal. The scenario includes expanded retirement savings access, broader automatic enrollment, periodic reenrollment, and an expanded Saver's Match.


Under the modeled policy scenario, 67% of Gen Z, millennial, and Gen X households are projected to have sufficient resources to cover retirement expenses, compared with 59% under the baseline scenario. That means eight more households out of every 100 could be more financially prepared for retirement.


“Access to a retirement plan is important, but access alone does not guarantee that workers will participate, or save enough,” said Spencer Look, associate director of retirement studies, Morningstar Retirement. “Our models show that automatic savings, could result in meaningful improvements to retirement security, especially for younger workers, and those disconnected from workplace retirement plans.”


Models indicate that younger households could stand to benefit the most, with retirement readiness rising by 12 percentage points for Gen Z, 10 percentage points for millennials, and 5 percentage points for Gen X. Lower-and middle-income households also could see larger gains than higher-income households.


Morningstar's researchers modeled the policy scenario as a whole and conducted additional analyses to assess how the results would differ if certain provisions were excluded. These analyses suggest that one provision alone was not driving the results. Sensitivity analyses incorporating higher opt-out rates and preretirement withdrawals continued to show improvements in projected retirement adequacy, although the magnitude of the gains varied with the assumptions.

Morningstar serves investors and financial professionals across the investment ecosystem, from individuals and advisors to asset managers, retirement plan providers, institutions, and issuers.
